title: Universal mod-p representation lifting obstruction
as_he_states: The rank-d universal obstruction vanishes for d≤1 and is expected nonzero for all d≥2.
plausible_today: Reduction GL_d(Z/p²)→GL_d(Fp) splits in rank 1 and the exceptional pairs (2,2),(2,3),(3,2).
state_of_art: Singla 2010, introduction p. 3 gives this classification, citing Sah1977 and Ginosar2001; the (2,2) splitting is independently certified here. The original Sah proof was not read.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: The claim is resolved; a short research run should document the original proof and its relation to the precise cotangent Ext² class.

title: Truncated Dieudonné dualizing bimodule and two coefficient actions
as_he_states: Construct a coefficient-functional duality through finite Dieudonné rings and their direct limit; the text warns about different W-actions.
plausible_today: Fix a single convention for W_n, truncation exponents, twisted left/right actions and transition maps, then formulate the compatible duality. The literal V-dual formula needs the ink check.
state_of_art: Oda 1969, Theorem 3.19 establishes Cartier/Dieudonné duality. Small exact ring computations here show why the truncation index matters. Codex cancels a finite-ring isomorphism that Pro leaves live.
why_open: The pages themselves flag the coefficient actions; cancellation differs between textual witnesses and cannot be decided without scans.
worth: Worth a concise convention audit after the scans are available, because it could settle several apparent contradictions at once.

title: Direct Gauss–Manin construction through a torsor of chain maps
as_he_states: The canceled sheet asks for a direct Gauss–Manin construction and proposes descent of local chain maps related by homotopies.
plausible_today: Use a specified derived enhancement with coherent descent data, or the later direct construction. Pairwise null-homotopies alone are not a complete theorem.
state_of_art: Illusie, Pisa 2015, §3.2 records the Katz–Oda 1968 construction. It does not identify this exact discarded torsor lemma.
why_open: The whole sheet is canceled; no reason for the cancellation is supplied.
worth: Useful for the manuscript commentary; a new research task should first recover the missing coherence conditions, not treat the draft as an established lemma.

title: Filtration-independent virtual inertia character of a p-divisible group
as_he_states: Assign equivariant K₀ classes to models of potentially-good filtration factors, and obtain an inertia trace independent of filtration and good-reduction extension.
plausible_today: For a fixed potentially-good object, finite inertia trace is compatible with extension. For the filtered construction, define the exact category and prove additivity/refinement independence before assigning a virtual character.
state_of_art: Tate full faithfulness is verified in Illusie §2.3.1; the modern elliptic finite-inertia framework appears in Dembélé–Freitas–Voight §3.2. No opened source established this exact K₀ construction.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a narrowly scoped exact-category reconstruction; the key first step is to specify which filtrations and equivariant models are allowed.

title: Brauer character from generic mod-p torsion
as_he_states: Try to identify the p-regular special-fiber inertia trace with the Brauer character of generic mod-p torsion, then retract the general claim.
plausible_today: The comparison works for an actual finite integral representation, such as a potentially constant p-divisible group, and fails without that hypothesis.
state_of_art: The manuscript counterexample μ_p∞ over Qp,p>2 is valid: good special-fiber inertia is trivial, mod-p cyclotomic inertia is not. This run checks that exact distinction.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly gives the obstruction and withdraws the unrestricted comparison.
worth: Resolved as a negative claim; retain it to prevent the later elliptic question from being mistaken for the same statement.

title: Can constant p-torsion conceal potentially-good elliptic inertia?
as_he_states: Withμp⊂K, do potentially-good elliptic curves with the same mod-p module have the same p-regular inertia character? A constant-torsion version is followed by an uncertain “faux par Tate” leader.
plausible_today: The answer is no even for p=5 and with a supersingular potentially-good curve. Finite WD/ℓ≠p inertia must be distinguished from raw T_p inertia.
state_of_art: proofs.md §1 gives an independent pair over K=F(5^(1/8)), F/Q5 unramified of degree 4: y²=x³+5⁴ and y²=x³−x have constant 5-torsion, but order 3 finite-inertia traces −1 and 2. The saved exact polynomial and F25 certificate checks the Hensel hypotheses. Modern type classification corroborates the finite inertia; Tate’s historical example is not identified.
why_open: The margin may record a negative answer by Tate, but its attachment is unresolved and no example is written.
worth: The mathematical question is refuted; the remaining useful task is historical identification of the margin and comparison with Tate’s actual communication.

title: Full F,V-compatible stratification of universal abelian deformations
as_he_states: Seek a functorial full k-stratification ofH¹_dR for all infinitesimal deformations, compatible withF,V and base change; expect ordinarity to be necessary.
plausible_today: Ordinary unit-F pieces have canonical local-system stratifications. Necessity must retain “all deformations” and specify compatibility and Hodge behavior; a constant nonordinary family does not address that universal question.
state_of_art: Katz 1981 gives ordinary formal parameters and explicit Gauss–Manin formulas. Illusie §4.2.1 gives the smooth deformation space. No exact necessity theorem for this formulation was found.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a short formulation task separating the Hodge-preserving unit-F stratification from Gauss–Manin before asking a necessity theorem.

title: Descending equality through Frobenius on a nilpotent base
as_he_states: The equality after Frobenius pullback is not enough if the base is nonflat; the next page uses the smooth universal deformation space.
plausible_today: Faithfully flat Frobenius detects equality of the subbundles; arbitrary Frobenius does not.
state_of_art: The two-line dual-number example independently confirms the obstruction. Formal smoothness supplied by the deformation theorem validates the author’s later repair.
why_open: This doubt is resolved by the author on the next page, not left open.
worth: No new research is needed; the commentary should join the warning and its continuation.

title: Polarization class, tangent map and transpose p-torsion map
as_he_states: Identify the middle de Rham component of a Néron–Severi class with the tangent map induced by its homomorphismA→A*, compatible with the transpose map on étale p-torsion.
plausible_today: The statement is expected with fixed covariant/contravariant conventions and the live corrected arrow direction.
state_of_art: Oda’s de Rham realization and crystalline Dieudonné duality provide the framework, but this run has not certified every sign in the manuscript’s altered diagram.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth checking jointly with the determinant normalization because the same duality conventions control both.

title: Unpolarized determinant line and Hasse compatibility
as_he_states: The top-trace/Hodge constructionω_A≃ω_A* should respect ordinary unit-F structures and Hasse invariants, and match the later mod-p Tate determinant.
plausible_today: A determinant-level compatibility with a fixed order of exterior factors is plausible. It does not imply an isomorphism of the full rank-g p-torsion modules.
state_of_art: The Hasse determinant criterion is exact in Caraiani, Lemma 4.1.7. Standard duality is established, but no source located gives this precise comparison of the author’s two normalizations.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: A few-hour normalization audit could settle a precise rank-one compatibility; first fix all determinant and biduality signs.

title: Explicit ordinary connected–étale extension data
as_he_states: Beyond perfect-base splitting, explicate the extension of multiplicative by étale factors over a general deformation base.
plausible_today: For ordinary A over algebraically closed k and artinian local R, the extension is encoded by bilinear maps T_pA_et×T_pA*_et→1+m_R; global bases require descent.
state_of_art: Katz, Theorem 2.1 answers this exact formal-neighborhood problem. Illusie’s discussion of Grothendieck’s letter 6.7 distinguishes a more general extension-deformation explanation.
why_open: Illusie says the extension-deformation part of the letter was not discussed in two later accounts; he does not give a reason for that omission.
worth: Established locally; a useful historical task would compare the letter’s general extension argument with the manuscript’s short question.

title: Polarization-independent ordinary Tate determinant
as_he_states: Prove thatdetT_p(λ)_et/√degλ is independent of polarization and identifies integral determinant lattices; an intermediate sign remains doubtful before scan 27.
plausible_today: The positive Rosati-symmetric proof and Cartier-self-dual kernel argument give the claimed determinant isomorphism for ordinary abelian varieties over perfect fields.
state_of_art: The author ends the sign argument “cqfd” and then proves integrality. Milne, Theorem 11.1 and §14 supply standard ingredients. Searches did not locate the exact normalized construction as a named later theorem.
why_open: The sign doubt is resolved within the same text; it did not remain open in these pages.
worth: Worth editorial reconstruction and a precise reference search, not another attempt to solve the already completed sign step.

title: Naturality with the correct dual variance
as_he_states: A broad functoriality objective is canceled, then the author identifies the wrong variance and usesu*⁻¹ for automorphisms.
plausible_today: The normalized determinant intertwines an isomorphism with its contragredient dual, and the two determinants for an isogeny multiply to its degree.
state_of_art: The product identity follows from ordinary étale/multiplicative duality. It does not give equality of individual determinants under unrestricted endomorphisms.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly identifies “mauvaise variance” and narrows the assertion.
worth: Resolved at the stated scope; retain the cancellation so the opening objective is not reinstated.

title: Biduality and product signs for the Tate determinant
as_he_states: Check compatibility withA**, products, and the sign of the duality identifications.
plausible_today: Product compatibility follows with ordered determinant factors and product polarizations. Biduality requires fixing the alternating-form convention; a convention-free sign is not supplied.
state_of_art: Milne’s duality and Rosati discussion supply standard background. No exact published sign computation for this normalization was located.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: A compact determinant-functor calculation is realistic in one research run; the scan check must precede assigning the final sign.

title: Transpose of the auxiliary F/V middle sequences
as_he_states: The two middle-degree sequences are “sans doute” transposes; the superscript/subscript ss refers to different stable operators.
plausible_today: Derived crystalline duality should identify them with the correct twist and adjacent torsion degree. A naïve same-degree transpose is not enough.
state_of_art: Illusie 1976, §2.4 gives crystalline duality/Gysin formalism. Katz, XXII, formula (3.3.4) supplies the F-stable augmentation. Uncertain F/V labels prevent a unique exact comparison.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a limited derived-duality diagram audit once the uncertain indices are read on the scans.

title: Integral weak Lefschetz with saturated cokernel
as_he_states: Admit an integral weak Lefschetz theorem strong enough that the critical restriction is injective with free cokernel for the smooth hypersurface sections under discussion.
plausible_today: The claim is established for all sufficiently high powers of a chosen ample line bundle under the coherent-vanishing hypotheses. The fixed-embedding all-degree version needs separate examination.
state_of_art: BMS, Lemma 2.12 proves the sufficiently ample form and cites Berthelot’s 1973 note. Rational weak Lefschetz does not imply saturation.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: High value: resolving the exact all-degree scope determines the domain of several subsequent manuscript formulas.

title: Injectivity of stable coherent restriction
as_he_states: Expectv:H^(n−1)(O_X)_st→H^(n−1)(O_Y)_st injective; state it forn2 and coherent-vanishing high degree.
plausible_today: The two stated cases are valid. The all-dimensional, all-smooth-hyperplane version is not certified here.
state_of_art: Stable-F/Artin–Schreier interpretation is in Katz, XXII; the high-degree assertion follows from the coherent long exact sequence. The surface case uses π₁ Lefschetz. Searches did not find a precise broader theorem.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a targeted étale-cohomological Lefschetz search because a positive answer simplifies the entire relative correction term.

title: Relative vanishing unit-F local system and constant kernel
as_he_states: On the generic maximum-rank open, the amended sequence should vary as finiteFp local systems with kernel coming from the base field.
plausible_today: Shrink for locally free stable images and base change, and control ker v. High degree with ker v=0 gives the claimed constant torsion kernel.
state_of_art: The unit-F dictionary and Hasse–Witt variation are established in Katz/Koblitz. The full relative integral sequence for exactly the manuscript’s initial open was not located.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a precise base-change construction; the first step is to separate stable-rank openness from crystalline saturation and constant-kernel hypotheses.

title: Eventual generic positive stable vanishing rank
as_he_states: Show generic stable coherent vanishing cohomology is nonzero for every sufficiently large degree; margin says section7 already proves it, but that section is absent.
plausible_today: The exact positivity statement holds for all projective equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay X of dimension≥1, with a degree bound depending on X and its embedding.
state_of_art: Katz, SGA 7 II, XXI, Theorem 1.4, pp. 374–376 is an exact published match. It is stronger in its allowable X than a smooth-complete-intersection-only result.
why_open: The local text claims an internal resolution. The supplied pages do not contain that proof; the later theorem is verified independently.
worth: Resolved; the remaining task is historical comparison of the absent section7 with the SGA proof, if that manuscript is supplied.

title: Unit roots and maximal motivic level
as_he_states: The nonzero unit-root condition should imply, and perhaps be equivalent to, motivic leveln−1 of generic vanishing cohomology.
plausible_today: A unit root obstructs positive coniveau. The converse needs a precise notion of level and additional input; it is not asserted for all X.
state_of_art: Katz, XXI, Corollary 2.2 proves eigenvalue divisibility for coniveau, and Theorem 4.2 proves a complete-intersection maximal-level result. These do not prove the general equivalence.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a formulation task only after recovering the author’s definition of level; otherwise an apparent conjecture may conflate distinct notions.

title: Comparing the crystalline torsion criterion with a characteristic-zero lift
as_he_states: IfX and polarization lift to characteristic 0, express the sufficient torsion condition for φ-bijectivity through p-adic étale cohomology of the lift.
plausible_today: Integral comparison gives inequalities and criteria under extra hypotheses; an unrestricted equality of crystalline and étale torsion is false.
state_of_art: BMS, Theorem 1.1 and §2.3 give the precise torsion-length comparison and strict examples. They do not directly settle the author’s stable-F condition.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a narrow comparison of the exact stable piece with integral p-adic realizations, keeping the known strict inequalities visible.

title: Examples where the revisedφ is not bijective
as_he_states: Find examples whereφ fails to be bijective; the earlier nonsurjectivity wording and product examples are canceled.
plausible_today: For a Serre free Z/p quotient surface with H¹_cris=0 and H¹_et(Fp)=Fp, the stable H² crystalline torsion gives a one-dimensional ker φ, under the admitted section hypotheses.
state_of_art: Berthelot–Esnault–Rülling, Remarks 9.2 verifies the historical quotient mechanism. The short crystalline implications are checked in proofs.md. No new high-dimensional geometric example is asserted.
why_open: The author replaces nonsurjectivity by nonbijectivity after correcting his exact sequence; the original product is crossed out.
worth: The surface example is adequate for the live request; a higher-dimensional construction would be a separate task with all cohomology and saturation assumptions checked.

title: Equality criterion and preceding-degree stable torsion
as_he_states: Assert thatφ-bijectivity is equivalent to equality in the stable coherent versus free-crystalline dimension inequality.
plausible_today: Under ker v=0 and absence of preceding-degree stable torsion the equivalence holds. In general the inequality defect is b+c whereas dim kerφ=c−dim ker v.
state_of_art: The exact elementary derivation in proofs.md §2 uses the opened base-change and stable-augmentation results. It shows a missing-hypothesis issue without claiming a geometric counterexample.
why_open: The manuscript does not discuss the extra preceding-degree term; whether an omitted hypothesis or a reading explains it is unresolved.
worth: High priority for the next scan-based commentary: first check whether a missing qualification removes the extra term.

title: FullGL_r(Fp) monodromy for fixed-X hypersurface sections
as_he_states: Is the varying stable coherent vanishing representation irreducible, or even full GL_r(Fp), for generic hypersurface sections of a fixed smooth projective X?
plausible_today: Specify geometric versus arithmetic image, degree range, rank, and fixed constant subquotients. Established full-image theorems for other parameter spaces do not imply this one.
state_of_art: Achter–Pries, Proposition 4.8 proves full mod p and p-adic monodromy on components of curve p-rank strata. Stienstra–van der Put–van der Marel studies specified unit-root families. Neither gives the exact arbitrary X theorem; searches recorded no matching general result.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Highest research interest, but one short run should test a concreteX and degree and audit arithmetic determinants before attempting the universal claim.

title: Growth of generic stable vanishing rank
occurrences: cote 4:9,1179,deleted growth replaced by positivity;12,1307–1312; P894-I036,P894-I041; P894-C065,P894-C074
as_he_states: The early growth expression is weakened to positivity, but unbounded rank is needed again for the final monodromy/congruence programme.
plausible_today: For a fixed smooth projective n-fold X of degree D, the generic stable vanishing rank has leading term Dd^n/n!, hence tends to infinity.
state_of_art: Koblitz I, §5, Theorem 1 explicitly states the leading term for a constructed section; Lemma 4 transfers the stable-rank lower bound to a generic open for Cohen–Macaulay X in sufficiently high degree, and Theorem 2 combines them. The unread displayed defect inequality is not needed for this conclusion.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: The unboundedness branch is settled; the remaining research obstacle is the separate monodromy question.

title: Every-open hypersurface point-count residues
as_he_states: Use fullGL monodromy and every residue as a matrix trace to force specified point-count congruences in every nonempty parameter open after suitable finite field extension.
plausible_today: The conclusion is conditional on geometric monodromy and allowed Frobenius cosets, with fixed cohomological contributions controlled after extending constants. Variable extension degrees are part of the statement.
state_of_art: The trace-surjectivity calculation is proved independently. Katz, XXII, Corollary 3.2 gives the mod p cohomological trace congruence. The missing all X monodromy prevents an unconditional conclusion.
why_open: No source located documents why this exact question remained open or was dropped.
worth: Worth a concrete-family experiment only after its monodromy is established; the elementary trace input is already complete.
